column2: Fill one row per published book. Update the sales columns at 30 and 90 days. The Verdict column is what stops you repeating a niche that does not pay.

column3: Review, metadata, upload. Be honest — this is the real cost.
What an hour of your time is worth elsewhere
= credit cost + (hours x hourly value). Edit the formula for your numbers.
Set this from your actual price and royalty band
= total cost per book / avg royalty. This is the number that matters.

column2: Beat break-even inside 90 days. Make three more books adjacent to this one.
Between half break-even and break-even. Give it one more title in the same niche before deciding.
Under half break-even at 90 days. Stop this niche. Three dead books in one niche is the signal to leave.
Kill a niche after three books that go nowhere. Persistence in the wrong niche is the most expensive habit in publishing.
When a book works, make the next three ADJACENT to it. Adjacent beats novel.
Four columns beat a dashboard. If you stop filling this in, the catalog stops teaching you anything.
Count your time. A book that breaks even on credits but cost you three hours did not break even.
